The site's Slurm cli_filter prints a two-line banner -- '[BILLING] loaded!' and '[BILLING] Re-emitting cost at job start!' -- on STDERR at every submission, so `2>&1` folded it into $out and the test failed although sbatch --parsable had SUCCEEDED. Measured on link 1 of the production chain: the link logged "sbatch did not return a job id -- chain not extended: [BILLING] loaded! / [BILLING] Re-emitting cost at job start! / 305318" while scontrol showed JobId=305318 JobState=PENDING Reason=Dependency Dependency=afterany:301099(unfulfilled) Partition=b200,l40s TimeLimit=23:30:00 -- the successor existed and was correctly wired (results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/production_chain/status_log.txt, monitoring read 1, 2026-09-04; the reader escalated the defect rather than editing an admitted script). Consequences: SUCCESSOR is empty on every link, so cancel_successor() can never fire and the three paths that exist to cut the chain early -- a deterministic pre-flight failure, a breaker trip and a storage stop -- are dead; the 'successor queued:' line P9 reads never appears; and every link logs 'chain not extended' over a chain it did extend. Chain continuity, the post-trip guard and the STOP brake are unaffected, each being enforced a second time at the top of the successor's own body. The same read exposed a second, independent counting defect in the reader: codes/eval/chain_status.sh P10 compared '[cycle N pre-gatekeeper]' guard-block headers against ALL 'scratch_guard: OK' lines, and a link makes one more guard call than it starts cycles (the wrapper's own '[chain link N pre-flight]' call), so the NOTICE fired on every healthy link and stayed silent when a per-cycle guard really did end without a clean verdict. Closes when: the id is read from sbatch's STDOUT alone and both --parsable shapes ('jobid' and 'jobid;cluster') are accepted; stderr is kept and logged verbatim rather than parsed; an sbatch that exits 0 without a readable id is a WARNING that consults the queue instead of declaring the chain unextended; only a non-zero sbatch exit reports 'chain not extended'; and chain_status.sh's P10 counts are aligned. candidate_result_row.claim: codes/loop/synchronous_loop_9x9.sh and codes/loop/export_model_for_selfplay_9x9.sh carry 'set -eu -o pipefail' in the body, so errexit, nounset and pipefail hold whether the file is executed or handed to `bash` -- the form loop.sbatch uses -- and a failure anywhere in the archive-staging section stops the loop instead of being followed by cycle 1 out of an incomplete archive. In codes/loop/loop.sbatch the .failcount accounting, the minimum-runtime penalty, the breaker and the scancel of the queued afterany successor live in one function, finalize(), run from an EXIT trap installed immediately after resubmit(), and finalize sorts the ways a link can end into five classes. A deliberate storage stop -- the loop exiting 3 WITH $BASEDIR/STOP present, the file the loop writes before that exit -- cancels the successor and spends no attempt. A scheduler termination -- SIGTERM to this wrapper, recorded by a TERM trap installed before the resubmit, or a 128+15 loop status on a link that has run at least KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS -- keeps the queued successor, which is the resume itself, and leaves .failcount alone unless the link completed cycles, in which case the run of consecutive failures is cleared. A SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight ends the link before the loop is launched. A loop failure already recorded when a later SIGTERM arrives is counted as the failure it is. A pre-flight failure counts, with the fast-failure penalty, and cancels the successor. A loop failure counts and cancels only when the breaker trips; an exit 3 without STOP is one of these. A cycle that ran and exited 0 resets the count, an exit 0 that never ran the loop leaves it, and a link that advanced $BASEDIR/.cycles_completed restarts the failure run, so KTG_MAX_FAILS means three failures with no completed cycle between them. Neither loop.sbatch nor synchronous_loop_9x9.sh contains a storage threshold or its own du/df/quotas.py measurement: both call codes/data_budget/scratch_guard.sh and honour its exit code, with no --root passed. The three upstream defect repairs (o09, o13 config half, o17) admitted in the earlier rows are unchanged, and a KTG_STAGE_ONLY dry run from the real scratch clone stages the same 80 files byte-for-byte before and after this repair. NOT covered: a SIGKILL end -- KillWait expiry, cgroup OOM, node failure -- runs no handler, writes nothing and simply lets the queued successor resume, shown by scenario M; a loop status 143 after the runtime floor is still read as a scheduler termination whatever caused it; a SIGTERM already seen outranks a deterministic pre-flight failure that follows it, self-correcting in one extra link; and a link that completes a cycle before failing never accumulates toward the breaker. Every chain-state integer under $BASEDIR -- .failcount, .chain_depth and .cycles_completed -- is now read through one function, read_counter() in loop.sbatch, which trims whitespace, requires a plain decimal of at most 18 digits and parses it with 10#, so a leading-zero value such as 08 or 09 is read as 8 or 9 rather than aborting the enclosing command list as an invalid octal literal, an unparsable value reads as 0 instead of aborting, and a value past 2^63 cannot wrap; an unparsable .failcount or .chain_depth additionally prints a WARNING line naming the file and the value that was read. finalize() therefore writes the count, writes .breaker_tripped and cancels the queued successor for every seed, and the wrapper reaches its resubmit for every seed. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATION (o36): that holds for every VALUE a state file can hold, and a corrupt .failcount costs at most one extra link because finalize() overwrites it with a plain decimal on the next failure (harness X8: abc, then 2, then 4 and the breaker on link 2; X8b at the slow-failure floor trips on link 3; X9: the corrupt value persists only across scheduler-terminated links, with a WARNING each). It does NOT hold when the file cannot be WRITTEN: no write of .failcount or .chain_depth is checked, so a .failcount that is a directory, unreadable or read-only is read as 0 (no WARNING when cat fails) and never advances -- every link prints 'chain continues' and queues its successor, a crash loop bounded only by KTG_MAX_CHAIN (X3, X4, X5); the same fail-open direction applies to the operator knobs, which are not read through read_counter: KTG_MAX_FAILS=abc makes every '-ge' test false so the breaker never trips (X10b: 2, 4, 6 with a successor each link) and KTG_MAX_CHAIN=abc removes the depth bound (X10c); KTG_MAX_FAILS=08 aborts finalize() at :375 after the count is written (X10a, the worker's residual). The loop's own CHANGE 10 writer carries the same trim / guard / width / 10# parse, so a seeded 08 self-heals to 9 on the next completed cycle instead of killing the loop after every cycle. No writer in codes/ can produce a padded value in the first place (no printf %0Nd, no seq -w; every write is an unpadded $(( )) result), so the exposure only ever needed a hand-edited or foreign-written file. Nothing here ran on a GPU or under a real scheduler. AMENDMENT (wave 3, R1/R6/R5). loop.sbatch:8 declares --cpus-per-task=32; the wrapper types no CPU count at all -- REQ_CPUS is KTG_CPUS_PER_TASK read from codes/loop/knobs_9x9.env, whose sha256 is logged at pre-flight; a knob file that is unreadable, or that carries KTG_MAX_FAILS/KTG_MAX_CHAIN/KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS, is not sourced at all, resubmit() then refuses to chain and the pre-flight exits 2; a granted SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK != KTG_CPUS_PER_TASK, or either engine cfg declaring a numGameThreads != KTG_NUM_GAME_THREADS, is a pre-flight failure (exit 2) that cancels the queued successor. The policy script named by mission.json compute.policyCheck passes at --gpus 1 --cpus 32 --partition b200. loop.sbatch starts codes/eval/stage_monitor.sh over $BASEDIR/monitor with its own pid as the sampling root after env.sh and the knob asserts (a missing sampler is a pre-flight failure), and stops it as the first statement of finalize() after FINALIZED=1, || true; synchronous_loop_9x9.sh retags the samples cycleN at the top of each cycle when $BASEDIR/monitor/monitor.run exists. The link samples at KTG_MON_PS_INTERVAL=1 / KTG_MON_GPU_INTERVAL=5; stage_monitor.sh's own defaults stay the smoke's 0.2 s / 2 s. synchronous_loop_9x9.sh runs codes/eval/check_pos_len_npz.py at loop start and again between selfplay and shuffle in every cycle, over the npz under $BASEDIR/selfplay newer than $BASEDIR/.pos_len_checked (all of them when the marker is absent), skipping cleanly at 0 files and touching the marker after a pass; a mismatch names the file and ends the cycle with exit 1 BEFORE the shuffle, instead of the train-time assert at data_processing_pytorch.py:91 a whole selfplay stage later. VALIDATOR QUALIFICATIONS (2026-09-04, record results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/wave3_prelaunch_repairs/validation.md). (i) The stray-knob guard is a line-anchored grep for NAME= at the start of a line: a knob file carrying a plain KTG_MAX_FAILS= / KTG_MAX_CHAIN= / KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS= assignment is refused before sourcing (V1f, V1i), but the spelling export KTG_MAX_FAILS=1 is sourced and retunes the breaker for that link (V1g: failcount 0/1, breaker on the first failure), and a $NAME reference to an unset variable anywhere in the knob file aborts the wrapper at :186 under set -u BEFORE the resubmit and BEFORE the EXIT trap, so that link ends with no successor and no accounting (V1j, the o26 class); both need an edit of the knob file, whose every non-comment line at HEAD is NAME=digits with no $ (o42). (ii) stage_monitor.sh stop kills the pids listed in monitor.pids without checking what they are: after a SIGKILLed link (no finalize, monitor.run and monitor.pids left behind, V6e) a successor that fails its pre-flight BEFORE its own start runs stop from finalize on the stale pids and kills whatever same-user process now holds them (V6g: an unrelated sleep of this user was killed); a successor that reaches start overwrites both files first. Needs SIGKILL plus a deterministic pre-flight failure plus pid reuse by a same-user process; bounded to one kill; recorded as o42 (b).
